title: Braided token-path trace and circuit visualizer + failover playbook
creator: Aisha Nadeem
description: Goal: build a braided token-path tracing capability and an associated dashboard that ties per-token latency decomposition to circuit states, admission decisions, KV cache hits, and multi-region failover events. This ticket covers the instrumentation, data pipeline, dashboard panels, and the operator playbook for on-call to triage token-level tail latency regressions during regional failover scenarios. Motivation: current dashboards surface p95/p99 per-request latencies but do not map token scatter across decode, KV lookup, admission, and fallback transitions. Without per-token path visibility, it's slow to attribute tail spikes to admission throttles, KV cache misses, or cross-region routing fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument token-scoped trace IDs that persist across ingress -> admission -> shard -> decode -> fallback transitions for sampled requests
Produce a token-path event stream with <5s write lag into our observability datastore for sampled traffic
Dashboard panels: token-level waterfall (prefix -> decode -> kv -> admission wait -> egress), braided circuit state overlay, p50/p90/p99 per-token by region and shard
Correlation panels: KV hit ratio vs token tail latency, admit-rate vs queue length, circuit open/half-open transitions aligned to token spikes
Runbook: step-by-step triage that uses the visualizer to identify whether to scale dedicated pools, open temporary region-failover, or flip canary fallback policies
End-to-end tests: synthetic harness that can reproduce a KV-miss-induced token p99 spike and validate dashboard shows the causal chain
notes_and_tradeoffs: Sampling: we will start with 0.1% token sampling to bound storage and iterate. Goal is to support on-demand ramp to 1% during incident investigations.
Storage: event stream will be kept 7 days in hot storage and 30 days in cold; full-token traces are heavy so we only persist token-level timings and circuit state transitions, not full decoded text.
Privacy: token content is redacted at the proxy before tracing; only timing and metadata (token index, kv_hit, shard_id, region, admission_decision) are recorded.
Overhead: instrumentation budget target is <2% added p99 latency for non-sampled requests. We will validate via microbenchmarks (ENG-331442 dependency).
Visualization: braided view is intentionally lossy to keep panels readable; operators can click into raw trace event stream for full details.
implementation_steps: 1) Add trace ID propagation hooks in ingress proxy and admission service (sampling flag + token index metadata)
2) Emit token events at shard ingress, KV lookup result, admission outcome, decode start/end, and fallback routing decision
3) Build a lightweight pipeline consumer to join events into token traces and write to observability DB
4) Create Grafana panels: braided waterfall, circuit overlay, correlation heatmaps, live trace inspector
5) Author runbook: triage steps, escalation path, and remediation playbook (scale, reroute, rollback)
6) Canary rollout to a single region and Dedicated pool with synthetic traffic validation
7) Full rollout across regions and add alerting tied to token-level SLO burn rates
risks: High cardinality of traces if sampling misconfigured — mitigated by strict sampling defaults and quota enforcement
Event reordering across the pipeline might complicate trace joins — mitigated by sequence numbers and eventual consistency window
Operator overload on playbook complexity — mitigated by clear dashboard affordances and automated suggestions in the runbook
